story_title: A Clinic Visit for Near Vision
task_instruction: Rewrite each active sentence in the passive voice.
paragraphs: An optometrist explains presbyopia, a common age-related change that can make close-up focusing more difficult. During a consultation, the clinician reviews possible next steps. {{red:An eye-care professional should assess changes in near vision.}} {{mask_1}} {{red:An optometrist can measure a person's near focusing ability with a reading chart.}} {{mask_2}} {{red:The clinic will schedule a comprehensive eye examination next week.}} {{mask_3}} {{red:Patients must tell the clinician about sudden changes in their vision.}} {{mask_4}}

After the examination, the clinician discusses options that may support near tasks. {{red:An eye-care professional may recommend reading glasses for some activities.}} {{mask_5}} {{red:The optician can adjust the frames to fit the patient comfortably.}} {{mask_6}} {{red:The clinic will explain the differences between single-vision and multifocal lenses.}} {{mask_7}} {{red:Patients should compare the available lens options with their clinician.}} {{mask_8}}

The clinic also provides guidance about follow-up care. {{red:Staff can send appointment reminders by email.}} {{mask_9}} {{red:An optometrist must check the prescription if close work remains difficult.}} {{mask_10}} {{red:The clinic may arrange another assessment after the patient tries the new lenses.}} {{mask_11}} {{red:Patients should report discomfort to the eye-care team.}} {{mask_12}}

The clinician answers questions about everyday activities and eye health. {{red:People can use brighter lighting for reading.}} {{mask_13}} {{red:An eye-care professional should investigate persistent headaches or blurred vision.}} {{mask_14}} {{red:The practice will give each patient written instructions about lens care.}} {{mask_15}} {{red:Patients must clean their lenses according to the manufacturer's guidance.}} {{mask_16}}

Before the visit ends, the optometrist reviews what will happen next. {{red:The receptionist will confirm the follow-up appointment by text.}} {{mask_17}} {{red:Patients may ask the clinic to explain any unfamiliar terms.}} {{mask_18}} {{red:The optometrist can discuss other options if the first lenses do not feel suitable.}} {{mask_19}} {{red:The clinic will update the patient's record after every examination.}} {{mask_20}} The clinician reminds patients that an eye-care professional can provide advice tailored to their needs.
